item.title: Indonesia volcano eruption disrupts hundreds of flights
item.description:
Ash cloud from Anak Krakatau affects hundreds of flights and some school and fishing activities Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international hub, affecting hundreds of flights as a result of an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano. Saturday’s eruption, which produced lava and booming sounds that were heard up to 435 miles (700km) away, according to Indonesia’s geology agency, also interrupted some school activities and fishing. Two more eruptions were recorded on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: What happens next after Lindsay Clancy's murder case ends in a mistrial?
item.description:
A jury narrowly deadlocked on Friday in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the 36-year-old Massachusetts woman accused of killing her children. Accused is the correct word in a legal sense. But it feels like the wrong one in a general sense, because it is not in doubt that in January 2023 she killed Cora, Dawson, and Callan Clancy, her three young kids. She admits as much. The jurors instead were tasked with analyzing her state of mind. Also not really in dispute is that Clancy was mentally unwell leading up to the killings—she had begged for help from those around her, gone to the emergency room, tried to check herself into a mental health facility, and said she was afraid to be alone. She was prescribed a laundry list of medications. She was, by all accounts, floundering. Did she ultimately plunge into a state of psychosis? Or was she just deeply anxious and depressed? Absent clairvoyance,…

Sources: BBC News, Reason, Slate, The Guardian

item.title: Philippines warns China may reassert itself amid US-South Korea drill cuts
item.description:
Volkswagen said it would slash 50,000 additional jobs — bringing the total to 100,000 by the end of the decade, the most in automotive history — as the German firm faces cutthroat competition from Chinese carmakers. European leaders have stepped up their vows to crack down on Chinese imports despite the potential blowback: A recent poll of 1,300 German companies showed 55% back tougher trade measures against China, even if they themselves suffer . European industry has rallied together as Chinese firms target sectors Brussels considers vital to its competitiveness. All the while, competition is getting stiffer: Xiaomi, maker of some of the most advanced EVs, said it would launch European sales next year , the South China Morning Post reported. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

Sources: Al Jazeera English, Semafor, The Guardian

item.title: Hawaii residents told to expect tropical storm conditions as Hurricane Lowell passes to the west
item.description:
Storm, which may make impact as soon as Monday, is third system in weeks to threaten state during hurricane season Hawaii has declared a state of emergency as powerful Hurricane Lowell makes its way toward the islands, with the first impacts expected as soon as Monday. The storm is the third system in just over three weeks to threaten Hawaii during an active hurricane season in the central Pacific. Lowell remained a category 3 hurricane early on Sunday morning, packing winds of 125 miles per hour while moving north-west at six miles per hour. Continue reading...

item.title: Falling ceiling debris at Kennedy Center may mire debate over renovations
item.description:
The Kennedy Center shared photos on Saturday that showed a partial ceiling collapse that happened during a rainstorm in the main hallway of the over 50-year-old performing arts building. Roma Daravi, vice president of public relations for the Kennedy Center, said the collapse underscored the need to close the building for renovations. "Another example of the urgent need to close for renovation and revitalization, as our Chairman President [Donald] Trump has championed," Daravi said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital, adding, "This structural failure stems from decades of neglect and deferred maintenance by the previous leadership, and there’s no justification for further delays in restoring America’s cultural center." item.title: The White House Made an Arcade Game Out of Deporting People
item.description:
As of September 3, the official White House website features a page titled “arcade,” where users can play games like Rio Run, in which the player—a pixelated, white, and balding Border Patrol agent—collects “border crossers” and adds them to a line of orange-jumpsuited figures trailing behind him. It’s a retro-cutesy version of the nightmarish and very real scenes of ICE agents forcing immigrants, chained in a line, onto deportation planes. Other games in the “arcade” include Build the Wall, a Tetris rip-off in which the user builds a wall to “protect the border from the coming horde.” (Tetris, in response to Build the Wall, has posted on Instagram that the company takes copyright infringement “very seriously.”) There’s also an eagle-themed game called Flappy Bill, and a MAHA-oriented school lunch game. It’s no surprise, considering the “wartime recruitment” framing of ICE’s current…
